comments.body:
Automated fix not possible with the current runtime contract and supplied certificates. This issue remains open and blocking for the requesting repo's numerical accounting/production activation.

The architecture review checked the cited OTP 28.5.0.7 sources: `erl_hl_timer.c:1098–1126` sets TIMED_OUT before expiry allocation/enqueueing; `1881–1883` queues cross-scheduler cancellation. `erl_proc_sig_queue.c:10644–10654` defers signal-buffer release through thread progress/aux work, and `erl_proc_sig_queue.h:1964–1973` frees at final reference-count zero. `gen.erl:251–280` deactivates a timed-out call's reply alias without acknowledging target consumption or native reclamation. Public demonitor/trace-delivery guarantees do not bridge these reclamation edges.

Neither request completion, scope retirement, additional DOWN waits, mailbox inspection nor zero snapshots can certify the requested native/deferred frontier. No history-independent envelope bound has been established here, and this is not evidence of a memory leak. Implementing a receipt based on those observations would incorrectly claim the missing guarantee.

Resolution needs either a source/ABI/profile-bound conservative envelope covering these native objects and TLS caller/delivery/tracking metadata, or runtime support for an acknowledged reclamation frontier. Missing/mismatched certification must fail closed in that future contract. This checkout's local OTP 28.5.0.5 / ERTS 16.4.0.5 also differs from the requesting profile's OTP 28.5.0.7 / ERTS 16.4.0.6.

We are continuing the independent functional fix in #98; that fix and its release do not resolve #97 or authorize managed production activation.

body.title: [internal] Supported bounded accounting or acknowledged control quiescence for managed H1
